tasks.short: Provide ophthalmic consultation to medical colleagues

steps.what: Read the ophthalmic consultation request and relevant patient records
Discuss the ophthalmic question and provide clinical consultation
Capture the consultation findings, advice and limitations
Write the ophthalmic consultation summary from clinician notes

loop.purpose: Express the clinician's captured advice in a summary
loop.input: Clinician notes and selected patient-record excerpts
loop.output: Summary draft linked to clinician notes
loop.check: Ophthalmologist checks laterality, findings, recommendation, urgency and uncertainty against the actual consultation
loop.stop: One correction then manual writing for unsupported or ambiguous statements
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates cannot fully express the case-specific advice

steps.what: Finish the consultation summary and check its intended clinical recipient
Send the final consultation summary to the requesting medical colleague

tasks.design: Configure the {OTHER} electronic patient-record system to show the consultation request beside relevant records. A bounded drafting aid expresses the ophthalmologist's captured advice; checking and sending the final internal summary remain separate steps.
tasks.previous_blocker: Finding relevant records and writing the consultation summary add time around the clinical discussion.
tasks.enabler_now: Native consultation views and clinician-note drafting can assist those fragments.
tasks.still_hard: Clinical advice depends on findings, uncertainty and what the requesting professional needs.
tasks.human_edge: The ophthalmologist owns the clinical interpretation and explains its limits.
tasks.altitude: Less retrieval and summary prose, with unchanged clinical responsibility.

evidence.claim: Autoscriber drafts consultation records with clinician validation; this supports documentation assistance, not automated ophthalmic advice or the proposed savings.
The specific typed-note workflow, native retrieval gain and labour estimate are model knowledge.

assumptions: Boundary includes record reading, consultation, capture, summary writing, checking and delivery. This scenario concerns a colleague inside the organisation; the conversation is not an external action.

The requesting clinician produces the existing request and patient reference. The ophthalmologist verifies identity, dates and source relevance in s1; missing information requires manual clarification.

The ophthalmologist captures question, eye or laterality, findings, recommendation and limitations in s3 at full time. The model receives those notes, not an assumed transcript; no recording or free transcription is introduced.
Test native consultation views and templates before custom code. Missing notes return to manual writing. The final send has its own gate; internal document saves have no approval or saving.
unknowns: Permission to process patient data with a drafting aid
research_questions: Does corrected summary drafting preserve the clinician's exact advice and uncertainty?

already_counted.description: Note capture, draft correction, final checking and delivery remain counted.

incremental.description: Audit summary errors and maintain permitted record access.

approvals.approved_version: Exact final summary, patient identity and requesting internal clinician checked before s6 delivery; changes void the check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100, R90, gross10 minus3 upkeep gives net7. Range1-4 assumes native retrieval and note-based summary drafting help; all clinical conversation and note capture remain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Collaborate with multidisciplinary professionals on patient care

steps.what: Review patient information before multidisciplinary care discussion
Collaborate with health professionals to decide the patient-care approach
Record multidisciplinary decisions, responsibilities and open questions
Update the patient-care plan from the recorded decisions
Communicate the final patient-care plan to the responsible colleagues

tasks.design: Use native multidisciplinary views and contextual care-plan fields in the {OTHER} electronic patient-record system. The ophthalmologist collaborates, records decisions, updates the plan and separately communicates the final version to internal colleagues.
tasks.previous_blocker: Navigation and repeating patient context add clerical work around team decisions.
tasks.enabler_now: Native patient-context views and short plan forms can remove repeated navigation and identifiers.
tasks.still_hard: Different clinical priorities must be reconciled for the individual patient.
tasks.human_edge: The ophthalmologist contributes eye-care expertise and negotiates a coherent approach.
tasks.altitude: Team judgement is unchanged; a little less time is spent finding and arranging records.

evidence.claim: Native patient-context views and structured care-plan forms can reduce navigation and repeated identifiers; the design and estimate are model knowledge.

assumptions: Boundary includes preparation, the team discussion, written decisions, care-plan update and internal communication. Each is separate; other professionals' unchanged meeting time earns no focal-role saving.
The ophthalmologist produces patient id, decision, responsible clinician, follow-up timing and unresolved question in s3 at full time. s4 uses that record; no free structured team output is assumed.
Existing record authors supply clinical source records through usual care; no extra extraction is transferred to them. Missing context requires ordinary record review and clarification.
Test native team views and contextual plan templates first. No automatic task allocation, order, alert or message is proposed. Same-system saves have no saving or self-gate.
unknowns: Responsibility for writing the care-plan sections
research_questions: Does contextual entry reduce repeated identifiers without shortening clinical decision capture?

already_counted.description: Decision capture, plan writing and final handoff checks remain counted.

incremental.description: Maintain contextual plan fields and native view links.

approvals.approved_version: Exact patient-care plan version, responsibilities and internal recipients checked before s5 communication; changes require recheck.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100, R93, gross7 minus2 upkeep gives net5. Range0-2 assumes native navigation and repeated-field gains; full discussion and clinical decision capture remain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prescribe corrective glasses or contact lenses

steps.what: Review refraction findings and relevant history before prescribing lenses
Determine the appropriate corrective lens prescription
Explain the lens prescription and discuss use with the patient
Write the corrective lens prescription in the clinical record
Issue the final corrective lens prescription to the patient

tasks.design: Configure a native refraction view and contextual prescription form in the {OTHER} electronic patient-record system. The ophthalmologist selects the correction, explains it, records actual prescription values and checks the exact version before issuing it.
tasks.previous_blocker: Record navigation and repeated patient identifiers add time around prescribing.
tasks.enabler_now: Native views and contextual forms can shorten those administrative fragments.
tasks.still_hard: The clinically appropriate correction depends on the individual patient's findings and needs.
tasks.human_edge: The ophthalmologist makes and explains the prescribing decision.
tasks.altitude: Prescribing authority and patient discussion remain unchanged.

reach.task: Understand the issued lens prescription and clarify ambiguities

evidence.claim: Native clinical views and contextual prescription forms can reduce repeated identifiers and navigation; no automatic lens selection or measured time gain is claimed.

assumptions: Boundary covers prescribing using available examination findings, patient discussion, prescription writing and issue. This design does not replace or shorten the clinical examination that produces those findings.

The existing examination workflow's clinician or ophthalmic technician produces refraction findings with patient id, eye, measurement value, unit and time during the examination. No additional transcription is required by this design; if absent, the ophthalmologist obtains and checks them manually within s1.

The ophthalmologist produces the selected prescription in s2 and captures its actual values and eye designation in s4, with time retained. The native form supplies patient context only, never inferred prescription values.
Test native views and forms first. The issue gate covers the exact prescription and patient; same-system saving of the draft prescription earns no saving or self-approval.
unknowns: Whether findings are already accessible in one view
Current prescription form defaults and actual entry time
research_questions: Can navigation and repeated identifiers be reduced while all actual prescription-value checking remains?

already_counted.description: Prescription entry and final issue checks remain counted.

incremental.description: Maintain native view links and check prescription form defaults.

approvals.approved_version: Exact patient identity, prescription values, eye designation and issued document checked in s5; changes invalidate the check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100, R93, gross7 minus2 upkeep gives net5. Range0-2 assumes repeated navigation and patient context currently require work; no clinical choice or actual prescription values are automated.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Review clinical findings and history relevant to ophthalmologic therapy
Select the appropriate ophthalmologic treatment or therapy
Discuss treatment benefits, risks and preferences with the patient
Write the ophthalmologic treatment prescription and patient-discussion record
Release the final treatment prescription into the internal care workflow

tasks.design: Configure relevant record views and a contextual treatment-prescription form in the {OTHER} electronic patient-record system. Selection and patient discussion remain human, followed by actual order writing and a separate final-version release to the internal treatment team.
tasks.previous_blocker: Navigation and repeating patient context interrupt the prescribing workflow.
tasks.enabler_now: Native views and contextual forms can reduce those clerical fragments without choosing treatment.
tasks.still_hard: Treatment suitability and patient preferences require clinical judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The ophthalmologist weighs options and retains responsibility for the prescription.
tasks.altitude: A little less record navigation; clinical decisions and accountability stay unchanged.

reach.task: Clarify the purpose and limits of a therapy referral
reach.learn: Complete treatment handoffs and patient goals

evidence.claim: Native contextual clinical forms can reduce navigation and repeated identifiers while the clinician retains treatment selection and actual prescription entry; the estimate is model knowledge.

assumptions: Boundary includes treatment review, selection, patient discussion, written prescription and release to the internal team. Treatment administration is not automated or counted as a saving.

Existing examination clinicians produce patient findings and history in ordinary care. The ophthalmologist reviews provenance, identity and date in s1; missing information requires manual checking there rather than a presumed suitability flag.

The ophthalmologist produces the treatment choice in s2 and captures treatment, indication, eye or site, necessary treatment details and patient-discussion outcome in s4. All actual clinical-value entry remains human; the form retains stable patient identifiers only.

Test native record views and contextual forms first. No automatic contraindication alert, therapy choice or downstream order is hidden. The final release has its own gate; an internal save itself earns no saving.
unknowns: Time spent on repeating context versus clinical prescription detail
research_questions: Can native context reduce repeated entry without changing the clinician's clinical-value capture or release checks?

already_counted.description: Clinical prescription capture and final release checks remain counted.

incremental.description: Maintain form context and inspect errors after configuration changes.

approvals.approved_version: Exact final patient, treatment prescription details, eye or site and internal treatment destination checked before s5 release; changes void the check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100, R92, gross8 minus3 upkeep gives net5. Range0-2 assumes avoidable navigation and repeated context; all treatment judgement, discussion and clinical-value capture remain human.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Clinical judgement, patient communication and prescribing stay with the ophthalmologist; selected lookup and record fragments become shorter.
reach: Clarify specialist consultation questions with optometrists
Improve explicit treatment handoffs with nurses and low vision therapists
skills_to_grow: Distinguish a draft save from a released clinical instruction
role.ambitious_version: An ophthalmologist with clearer records and handoffs and less repeated clerical work, while retaining every clinical decision.
